title: Refactor interaction primitives into a Figma variable library for cross-surface consistency
creator: Asha Patel
description: Consolidate and refactor interaction primitives (spacings, elevation, focus/hover states, micro-interactions) into a single Figma variable library and token map that can be consumed by the Console design system. Goal is to eliminate inconsistent touch targets and motion across dashboards, rollouts rail, and cost views; enable single-source-of-truth for runtime engineers and speed up front-end implementation.
acceptance_criteria: A single Figma file (Variables + Components) exists with clearly named primitives and example usages for Dashboard cards, Rollout rails, and Cost metric chips
Token naming follows agreed canonical taxonomy (surface.{elevation|interactive}.{state}) and exported tokens match front-end token schema in console-variables.json
Design handoff includes CSS/JS token mapping table, code-ready component snippets, and accessibility notes (touch target sizes, reduced motion)
Two cross-discipline reviews completed: Design-Engineering pairing review and Product sign-off; feedback items either resolved or added as tracked follow-ups
Migration guide drafted for replacing legacy tokens in at least three high-impact Console screens (Dashboards, Rollouts, Cost Explorer)
decisions: Adopt surface.{level} naming instead of previous 'elevation' alone to clarify intent for z-order vs tactile surfaces
Use Figma Variables feature (not only styles) to support platform-level token exports; canonical source will be the Variables page in the design file
Prefer motion presets with reduced-motion alternatives; default to 'subtle' for analytics surfaces where frequent updates occur
Use 44px minimum touch target for interactive chips and 32px for inline controls per mobile considerations, documented in accessibility notes
notes: 2025-02-18: Kickoff meeting with PM and Eng. Agreed scope focused on primitives rather than full component rewrite.
2025-02-21: Inventory completed across 18 screens; identified 27 conflicting tokens and 11 inconsistent micro-interactions.
2025-02-25: Prototype created for 'rollout rail' with new token variables; used interactive Figma prototype to demonstrate focus states and density variants.
2025-02-27: Paired session with frontend (Jonah Kim) to validate token export format and mapping to console-variables.json schema.
2025-02-28: Accessibility review with UX Research recommended increasing contrast for metric pill text at small sizes; update applied to variable palette.
2025-03-01: Created migration checklist and flagged two high-risk screens for staggered rollout to avoid release coupling.
2025-03-02: Engineering requested a fallback plan for older components that cannot immediately consume Variables; added CSS shim guidance.
2025-03-03: Design review scheduled; most feedback minor naming tweaks and an ask to add example for 'dense cost table' variant.
review_feedback: PM (Liam O'Connor): Ensure migration doesn't change user-facing spacing on customer dashboards during the A/B rollout; prefer visual parity where possible
Frontend (Jonah Kim): Token export should include numeric tokens for spacing (e.g., spacing.8 = 8) so runtime batching heuristics can compute container thresholds
Accessibility (Rina Shah): Add explicit focus visible token and a keyboard-only interaction demo for the rollout rail
Design Lead (Evelyn Park): Rename 'interactive.surface' to 'surface.interactive' for lexicographic grouping in the variables UI
Productionization (Marisol Vega): Add transitional CSS shim pattern and include a small migration script example linked in handoff
follow_ups: ENG-8421: Backend to add token endpoint for runtime feature flags (dependency)
DES-20990: Component gallery refresh to use new Variables (sub-issue)
PM-401: Coordinate rollout dates with release team and flag on-call for first week
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Publish Variables file and update token export script (1 week)
Phase 2: Migrate low-risk components and add CSS shim (2 weeks)
Phase 3: Migrate high-traffic dashboards behind feature flag and monitor metrics for layout regressions (1 release cycle)
Phase 4: Remove legacy tokens and finalize docs; ship console-2025.03
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Visual regressions on high-traffic customer dashboards. Mitigation: staggered rollout and A/B visual diff snapshots.
Risk: Frontend build pipeline incompatible with Figma Variable export format. Mitigation: provide intermediate JSON token file and shim.
Risk: Reduced-motion users experience janky transitions if motion tokens change. Mitigation: add explicit reduced-motion token and test with assistive tech team.
